//: THE RATCHET. Read scripts/check-rtl.mjs section 3c before touching this file.
why: check-rtl exited 1 all of 2026-08-16 and was in no npm script that anything ran, so four agents shipped uncatalogued copy and the counter did not move. This file is what makes it a gate again: verify runs check-rtl --gate, which fails on NEW debt only. Existing debt is a scheduled migration with named owners (comms/handoffs/M8-rtl-arabic-pdpl-checker-blind-spot.md). Raising a number here is a reviewable act; a checker that quietly re-baselines itself is a checker that measures nothing.
howToLower: Catalogue the strings, then re-run node scripts/check-rtl.mjs --json and paste the new totals here in the same commit as the fix.
raisedBecause: THE LENS WIDENED. NOTHING GOT WORSE. The M15 acceptance verdict falsified two silences in the copy scan and a third was found alongside them; fixing all three made pre-existing strings visible that the checker had never been able to see. A raise here is only ever honest if it says which of these two things happened, so both numbers are measured separately below rather than netted.

raiseArithmetic.howTheSplitWasMeasured: The widened check-rtl.mjs was run against a clean `git worktree` at 8e77a23 — the exact tree fidelity-qa-reviewer measured at 261. It reported 316. Every one of the 55 therefore predates this session and none of it belongs to the two agents editing concurrently; the only delta between that worktree and this tree is the 8 strings catalogued out of ProjectSwitcher.tsx. A raise measured against the working tree would have been unable to tell those apart, which is how a widened lens launders new debt.
theThreeSilences: A template literal with ZERO interpolations was invisible: identical prose was a FAIL as aria-label="…" and silent as aria-label={`…`}. The `assembled-template` blind spot justifies itself on `${a} · ${b}` joins; a zero-interpolation template has no such defence and is simply a string.

MACHINE_CONTEXT was matched against the raw line, and it holds `to`, `it`, `as`, `id`, `key`, `name`, `type` and `test` — identifiers, and also ordinary English. So a sentence could suppress its own finding: 'Everything on screen is scoped to it.' was silent and 'Everything on screen is scoped.' was a FAIL. This is the biggest of the three by count and nobody had named it.

Nothing observed a missing Arabic plural class. `Plural` makes zero/one/two/few/many optional, so deleting the Arabic dual compiled, passed the gate and did not move the coverage figure by one. Now `missing-plural-class`, and it is a hard fail rather than a ratchet entry.

hardFails: missing-catalogue · missing-translation · missing-plural-class · orphan-translation do NOT go through the ratchet, and must never appear in byRule or byModule below. The ratchet asks 'did this number go up', which is the wrong question for a property whose only acceptable value is zero: the moment a baseline RECORDS one of these, the gate accepts it forever and accepts a different one in its place. Falsified, not reasoned — with missing-translation:1 recorded here, deleting 'shell.tab.chart' from strings.ar.ts gave regressions [], the word 'holding', and (before the hard-fail set existed) exit 0, with an English key untranslated.

notCounted.//: Recorded, never compared — these are the checker's declared blind spots at the moment this baseline was taken, so a later reader can see whether a category moved. `null` means not measurable from source, which is not zero.
